scope: Consumed-Dev conditional mechanism experiment only. It is not a representative Pass@1 estimate, SOTA result, leaderboard claim, or protected evaluation.
scientific_question: After a strong Agent has formed a complete deployment program, does executable public-goal feedback from running that program in a clean target-state environment cause more terminal EnvBench Official passes than an otherwise identical tool response that withholds the target-state evidence?

selection.source_prefix: The first 18 positions attempted by the frozen strong-A Census83 v6 execution.
selection.rule: Include every position whose valid A1 strong-Agent session emitted an admissible complete program and whose post-session public clean replay ended in a semantic Fail. Exclude A1 clean-replay Pass, infrastructure_error, pre-candidate failure, and unattempted positions.
selection.outcomes_used: Only the pre-existing A1 candidate-formation and public clean-replay status are used to define the opportunity cohort. Prior B, A2, and Official outcomes are not used to include or exclude a position.
selection.selection_limit: This is a conditional repair-opportunity cohort. It cannot estimate prevalence or end-to-end gain over all EnvBench projects.

arms.C_withheld: One fresh gpt-5.6-sol xhigh session receives the common prompt, construction shell, submit_and_replay tool schema, and one or more normal model requests. When it submits a complete program, the tool records the exact bytes but returns status=withheld and null target-state fields. The Agent must return the submitted program unchanged.
arms.T_real: One fresh gpt-5.6-sol xhigh session receives the identical prompt, construction shell, submit_and_replay tool schema, and normal model requests. The tool executes the submitted complete program in a fresh clean target state and returns only internal public-goal and integrity evidence to that same still-running session. Semantic Fail may be repaired and resubmitted.
arms.unique_causal_difference: The field values returned by submit_and_replay after candidate formation: real public clean-execution evidence versus typed withheld values. Model, reasoning effort, initial source, image, prompt, tool names and JSON shape, construction access, candidate boundary, safety limits, and post-episode Official evaluation are matched.

execution.prompt_visibility: Both arms are told that the common tool can return pass, fail, unknown, infrastructure_error, or withheld; neither arm is identified to the Agent before the tool result.
execution.session_requirement: The submit call, returned payload, any repair reasoning, and any revised submit call must occur before the same Codex session terminates.
execution.construction_hosts: Pair members use the same host. Odd pair indices use Spark and even pair indices use AgentHub. At most one active pair member per host.
execution.arm_order: Fixed alternating order: C first for odd pair indices and T first for even pair indices.
execution.target_state_replay: Fresh exact-revision checkout and EnvBench Python image, using the public executable goal and repository-effect audit only.
execution.official: After the Agent session terminates, execute the final submitted program with EnvBench Official. Never return Official output to either Agent.
execution.infrastructure_retry: For an in-session infrastructure_error, retry the unchanged program once. For post-episode Official infrastructure censoring, retry unchanged bytes up to three total attempts. Never convert an infrastructure retry into a semantic repair.
execution.resource_policy: Token, time, and cost are measured outcomes, not success thresholds. Existing large safety caps remain unchanged.

eligibility.pair: Both sessions complete, each calls submit_and_replay at least once, each final program matches its last submitted bytes, no Official result enters either session, and both final programs receive a valid terminal Official outcome after allowed unchanged infrastructure retries.
eligibility.treatment_activation: The first admissible real replay returns semantic Fail, the failure is delivered before the treatment session ends, and a later submitted complete program differs from the failed program.
eligibility.supporting_causal_chain: Treatment activation is followed by a program change that addresses the returned counterexample, T Official-passes, and C Official-fails.
eligibility.pre_candidate_failure: Record separately and exclude from the conditional pair contrast; do not relabel it as replay repair.
eligibility.candidate_or_boundary_invalid: Record and exclude under the same shared candidate policy without replacing the project.
eligibility.infrastructure_censored: Record separately and exclude from the paired semantic denominator without replacing the project.

analysis.primary_endpoint: Paired EnvBench Official Pass for the final program from each arm.
analysis.primary_contrast: T-exclusive Official wins versus C-exclusive Official wins, with the exact paired discordance table and two-sided exact McNemar result.
analysis.mechanism_analysis: For every T replay, report status sequence, whether feedback arrived before session end, exact program changes, failure family, and whether Official passed. First-replay Pass validates a program but is not failure-conditioned repair evidence.
secondary: input, cached input, output, and reasoning tokens
analysis.prior_exposure_note: These projects are consumed and several have historical treatment trajectories. The new runner contains no case-specific rules or cross-case memory, and Codex memories remain disabled. Results qualify the mechanism only and do not support held-out generalization.

decision_rule.promote_for_independent_dev_replication: At least two valid supporting causal chains in at least two non-equivalent failure families, more T-exclusive than C-exclusive Official wins, and no fidelity contradiction.
decision_rule.retain_narrow: One valid supporting causal chain, or multiple chains confined to one failure family. Do not open protected evaluation.
decision_rule.kill_as_core: After at least six valid pairs, T-exclusive wins do not exceed C-exclusive wins and no valid supporting causal chain exists, or real replay systematically increases terminal failures without a compensating Official gain.
decision_rule.insufficient: Fewer than six valid pairs or fewer than two treatment activations without a kill condition. Complete the frozen cohort before selecting any new cases.

implementation_failure_policy: A pre-Agent or tool-wiring failure may be corrected and rerun from a fresh session with no prior trajectory supplied. Semantic outcomes may not be erased or rerun by changing code, prompt, boundary, or protocol.
safeguard_note: No new hash, frozen contract, or runtime gate is introduced. Existing candidate and repository safeguards remain active. Final-program equality with the last tool submission is recorded for adjudication rather than enforced as a new generation gate.
